properties.state: {"decision":"UNDECIDED as a vocabulary question, but MUCH SMALLER than it looked, and the skill that tests it is BUILT (2026-07-25, the brainstorm skill). REFRAMED by Anthony the same day, and the reframe was the useful part: what he and his brother were asking for is not a staging GATE, it is a KIND. \"I think I now realize what my brother's idea was trying to say — it is like a brainstorming session where you can work through ideas without committing to anything yet. These would be more like 'ideas' not yet fleshed out and could be held in the graph as just that, 'brainstorming ideas'.\" That dissolves the contradiction this decision was opened over: the git study rejected the index because a gate between every edit and the graph is where intent goes to be forgotten, whereas a brainstorm is the opposite move — the idea DOES enter the graph, immediately, labelled as what it is. Nothing waits outside, so nothing is lost, and the design still never claims a half-formed thought as intent. THE FINDING THAT SHRANK THE QUESTION, from reading the detector while building the skill: the existing vocabulary ALREADY tells a musing from a choice, and a computation already reads the difference. `detect_gaps` raises `undecided_decision_point` only on a proposed Decision holding TWO OR MORE REGISTERED ALTERNATIVES — a fork with a real design export behind each branch (detect.rs: `alts.len() < 2 { continue }`). A proposed Decision whose options live in its prose therefore raises NO gap at all. So brainstormed ideas are silent by construction, and the nudge to choose arrives exactly when the ideas stop being ideas: register_alternative turns an option into a fork, and being asked to decide a fork is correct. Nobody has to remember which is which, and no label was needed to get it. WHAT A `brainstorm` KIND WOULD STILL BUY, and it is now a short list rather than the four-item one recorded yesterday: (a) delivery and certainty counts already exclude Decisions, so nothing is owed there; (b) gap silence is already delivered, per the finding above; (c) what remains is RETIREMENT — an idea nobody has touched in months could be surfaced as a candidate for tidying rather than sitting in the decision list forever, which is a real computation and the only one left standing; and (d) READABILITY — a person scanning 70-odd Decisions cannot tell at a glance which were choices and which were musings, which the skill currently answers with a sentence of prose inside the node rather than with a queryable property. PRIOR FRAMING, KEPT because it was true when written: the ask read as an opt-in \"think first, commit later\" mode; a session making no write calls IS rubber-ducking and the read tools are the ducking aids; and the narrow question was what happens at the END — which the skill now answers as a PROMOTION step, not a commit step.","name":"OPEN — do half-formed ideas get a place in the graph, distinct from things the design asserts?","rationale":"Raised by Anthony and his brother 2026-07-24, reframed by Anthony 2026-07-25, and the skill built the same day on his word (\"go ahead with the brainstorm skill\"). Built as a SKILL and not a schema change deliberately: it tests the practice at the cost of prose, and if the practice sticks the vocabulary question can be answered with evidence instead of taste — whereas a new node type or an enum value would have bought an upgrade doc and a foundation-migration checklist for a noun nobody had used yet. The evidence for the feature is this session itself: Anthony produced four isolation ideas he explicitly did not want to commit to, and the only home for them was a proposed Decision. That worked (dec:concurrent-work-isolation), which is why this is not urgent; it is also a slightly wrong fit, since a Decision node is meant for a choice someone is actually facing, and knowing exactly which part of the fit is wrong is what the finding above now pins down. Left PROPOSED because two of the four original arguments for a kind have dissolved and the remaining two (retirement candidates, at-a-glance readability) are real but small — and whether they are worth a schema change is Anthony's call, not a judgement to be made by the agent that just wrote the skill.","status":"proposed"}
